title: A Map Before the Laser

patient.name: Mr Marcus Lim Jun Hao
patient.presenting_complaint: Self-referred enquiry for LASIK suitability — Pentacam corneal tomography requested

history.hpc: Mr Lim says 'I very sian of wearing glasses already, want to check whether I can do LASIK.' He is highly short-sighted and wants to explore refractive surgery. No eye pain, no eye rubbing habit reported, no previous eye surgery. The doctor ordered a Pentacam corneal tomography scan to assess the cornea before deciding on refractive surgery suitability.
history.pmhx: Myopia with astigmatism. No medical history. No history of keratoconus or eye rubbing.
history.family_hx: No known family history of keratoconus
history.social_hx: Office worker, long screen hours. Non-smoker. Has not worn contact lenses recently.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Clear corneas, no scarring or signs of corneal ectasia on slit lamp
examination_findings.fundus: Myopic fundus, no retinal tears or detachment noted on the report provided

pentacam.anterior_posterior_elevation: Within normal limits, no localised elevation island
pentacam.result: Regular astigmatism, normal pachymetry and elevation maps, no tomographic signs of keratoconus or forme fruste; handed to doctor for refractive surgery decision

diagnosis: Pentacam corneal tomography completed with acceptable quality specification on both eyes. Pachymetry, keratometry and anterior/posterior elevation maps are within normal limits with regular astigmatism and no signs of keratoconus or forme fruste keratoconus. The maps were provided to the doctor to inform the LASIK suitability assessment — the technician does not make the surgical decision.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and confirm both eyes are to be scanned for refractive assessment
Confirm any contact lens wear has been stopped for the required washout period before mapping
Explain the procedure: non-contact, look at the central target, the camera rotates and takes a few seconds, no touching the eye
Enter patient details and select the corneal tomography scan
Position the patient at the chinrest, align on the corneal apex and ask the patient to open the eye wide and fixate
Capture and check the quality specification (QS = OK); repeat captures with poor quality, blinks, or misalignment
Generate the pachymetry, keratometry and elevation maps and provide to the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to assess corneal thickness, elevation and topography to determine suitability and treatment depth
If any ectasia risk is flagged, further assessment or alternative procedures may be considered
Document any recent contact lens wear that could affect the maps
patient_education: Explain that the scan maps the shape and thickness of the cornea, which is essential to decide if LASIK is safe
Reassure the patient it is quick, painless and does not touch the eye
Advise that contact lenses must be left out for the advised period before mapping to avoid distorting the cornea

key_points: Confirms patient identity and that both eyes are to be mapped
Checks and confirms the required contact-lens washout period before scanning
Asks about eye-rubbing / keratoconus risk relevant to refractive surgery
Explains the non-contact tomography procedure to the patient
Aligns on the corneal apex and obtains steady fixation with the eye open
Checks the quality specification (QS = OK) and repeats poor-quality captures
Captures pachymetry, keratometry and anterior/posterior elevation for both eyes
Recognises blinks/misalignment as causes to repeat the scan
Understands the purpose of corneal tomography in refractive surgery screening
Recognises pachymetry and elevation maps as key to ectasia screening
Does not decide surgical suitability independently — provides maps to the doctor
Identifies recent contact lens wear as a confounder of corneal shape
Obtains good-quality maps (QS OK) for both eyes
Repeats poor captures rather than accepting low quality
Provides complete maps to the doctor for the suitability decision
Educates the patient on contact lens washout and the purpose of the scan
